blocks.heading: Attracting, choosing and developing staff
blocks.text: Recruitment attracts suitable applicants for a vacancy; selection chooses the most suitable applicant using relevant criteria. Induction introduces the new employee to the business, colleagues, procedures and role. Further training develops the skills and knowledge needed for work. Start by identifying the vacancy and preparing a job description and person or job specification. Advertise through suitable channels, assess applications consistently, shortlist, interview or use relevant work tests, then appoint and introduce the worker. Develop capability and review progress after appointment. Training can be on-the-job in the work setting or off-the-job away from normal work tasks. These methods differ in resources and suitability; attracting an applicant is not the same as developing a current employee.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Omi Foods appoints a new order clerk and then teaches that person to use its order system. Advertising and gathering applicants belong to recruitment, comparing applicants belongs to selection, introduction to the workplace is induction and developing system capability is training. A course does not itself attract applicants to a vacancy.

blocks.heading: Recruitment
blocks.text: Recruitment identifies a vacancy and attracts a pool of suitable applicants. Define the duties and relevant person criteria before selecting a channel such as an internal notice or external advertisement. Internal recruitment can use known staff and offer progression but restrict the pool; external recruitment can bring new skills but requires assessment and introduction. The aim at this stage is suitable applications, not yet a final appointment.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Hela Print needs an additional customer clerk. It should specify the role and advertise through channels likely to reach suitable people. Announcing a vague vacancy without duties makes it harder for applicants to judge their fit.

blocks.heading: Selection
blocks.text: Selection evaluates applicants and chooses the person best suited to the stated job criteria. Use the application evidence to shortlist consistently, interview relevantly and use an appropriate task or skills test where useful. Check stated qualifications or references as appropriate before making an offer. A friendly interview alone may not show accuracy or competence. The process should use job-related evidence rather than unrelated impressions.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Eya Goods needs accurate order entry. Shortlisted applicants complete a brief original practice entry task and explain how they check it. The task provides evidence of accuracy relevant to the vacancy. Compare the same essential criteria rather than choosing solely on confidence in conversation.

blocks.heading: Induction
blocks.text: Induction training is an introduction given to a new employee, explaining the firm’s organisational structure, activities and procedures. It can include colleagues, reporting, safety arrangements, role expectations and where to ask for help. It can reduce uncertainty and avoidable early mistakes. It is not a substitute for learning every specialist task. On-the-job and off-the-job methods can support later skill development according to need.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Kena Repairs introduces its new assistant to the supervisor, workplace layout and procedure for reporting customer problems. This is induction because it helps the new worker understand the organisation and settle into the role. Further system practice may still be required.

blocks.heading: Training
blocks.text: Training develops the knowledge and skills required for work. Identify the capability gap, set a learning objective, choose a suitable method, provide practice and feedback, then check whether the worker can perform the task. On-the-job training uses workplace guidance; off-the-job training provides learning away from normal duties. The goal is capability, not attendance alone. Production or service improvements depend on applying the learning with adequate equipment and support.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Ota Stores’ clerk repeatedly enters incorrect collection dates. Teach and practise the date-checking procedure, then assess correct use on sample bookings. A certificate of attendance alone would not show the error has been resolved.

blocks.heading: Keeping the ideas apart
blocks.text:
Explain the difference: fictional Omu Goods advertises a vacancy, then later teaches the appointed worker to use its stock system.

Advertising attracts applicants and belongs to recruitment. Teaching the appointed worker develops capability and is training. Selection chooses between applicants; it is another stage. A business may need both recruitment and development, but one is not a definition of the other.

blocks.heading: Worked practice: Recruitment materials and training suitability
blocks.text:
Fictional Eha Repairs recruits a bookings assistant. The role involves accurate customer records and clear messages, not technical repairs. A competent supervisor can teach the safe booking system with practice records. Management compares a focused advertisement based on relevant criteria with a vague advert demanding an unnecessary technical qualification.

a(i) Define recruitment. [2]
a(ii) State two components of a job advertisement. [2]
b State two elements of induction. [2]
c Explain why supervised on-the-job learning could suit Eha’s assistant. [6]
d Evaluate the focused advert against the vague qualification-heavy alternative. [8]

a(i) Attracting suitable applicants for a vacancy. a(ii) Role title and application method with closing date. b Introduction to reporting relationships and relevant workplace procedures. c The supervisor has the needed expertise and practice records limit the impact of mistakes. Learning on the actual system makes the skills directly relevant, while feedback can check accuracy before live work. d A focused advert communicates real duties and essential criteria, attracting relevant applicants and supporting consistent selection. The technical qualification is unrelated to the stated administrative work and may exclude capable people. Choose the focused advert, with clear hours, application details and closing date; verify accuracy through suitable selection rather than assuming an irrelevant qualification proves it.

blocks.heading: Worked practice: Recruitment materials and training suitability
blocks.text:
Fictional Eha Repairs recruits a bookings assistant. The role involves accurate customer records and clear messages, not technical repairs. A competent supervisor can teach the safe booking system with practice records. Management compares a focused advertisement based on relevant criteria with a vague advert demanding an unnecessary technical qualification.

a Explain how Eha’s description, specification and selection process should connect. [8]
b Evaluate whether its available workplace learning is preferable to an unspecified external course. [12]

a The description states recording, diary and customer duties. The specification translates them into accuracy, communication and computer skills. Applications and a practical booking task can then provide evidence against those same criteria. Consistency prevents selecting for an unrelated technical qualification while neglecting actual record accuracy. b Workplace learning uses the actual system, an available competent supervisor and safe practice records, giving relevant feedback without an external course’s travel and fees. It takes the supervisor’s time and needs structured learning rather than being left to watch. An external course can offer specialist teaching but is not automatically relevant. Choose supervised workplace learning with competence checks on these facts; change the approach if expertise is unavailable or the task requires facilities the workplace lacks.

blocks.heading: Worked practice: Recruitment materials and training suitability
blocks.text:
Fictional Tula Goods appoints a new clerk to use its simple stock system. A competent colleague is available, and errors can be contained in practice records before live use. It compares supervised on-the-job learning with an external course on a different system.

Evaluate Tula’s two learning options under the original facts. Give a concise plan. [12]

Need: accurate use of the actual stock system. Workplace option: competent colleague, contained practice errors and direct relevance; requires time and clear steps. External option: structured teaching but a different system and extra absence or fees. Judgement: choose supervised on-the-job learning and check competence before live use. Induct the new clerk as well; introduction and skills development have related but distinct purposes.
